title: Armor Senior Sergeant
raw_text:
10-19Z. MOS 19Z--Armor Senior Sergeant, CMF 19 (Effective 202411)
    a. Major duties. The Armor Senior sergeant serves as principal NCO in an Armor Company,
Cavalry Troop, or operations staff within in Combined Arms Battalion, Cavalry Squadron, or
higher-level organizations. Duties for MOS 19Z at each level of skill are as follows:
       (1) MOSC 19Z5O. The Armor Senior Sergeant serves as the principal NCO in an Armor
Company, Cavalry Troop, or Operations Sections of a Combined Arms Battalion, Brigade Combat
Team, or higher-level organizations. Provides tactical and technical guidance and professional
support to subordinates and makes recommendations to superiors in the accomplishment of their
duties. The key developmental position for MOS 19Z5O is a First Sergeant.
       (2) MOSC 19Z6O.
           (a) SGM: Serves as principal noncommissioned officer in a Combined Arms Battalion,
Cavalry Squadron, or higher to supervise the processing of operations and intelligence
information. Provide tactical and technical guidance to subordinates and professional support to
both subordinates and superiors in accomplishment of their duties. Plans, coordinates, and
supervises activities pertaining to organization, training and combat operations. Edits and
prepares tactical plans and training material. Coordinate implementation of operations, training
programs and communications activities.
           (b) CSM: Serves as the principal advisor to the Commander (Battalion/Squadron, and
higher-level unit) on all enlisted issues and is primarily focused on the training, maintaining,
caring, and leading of the unit's Soldiers, facilities and equipment. Assists the Commander in the
implementation of command policies and establishes and enforces standards related to the
appearance and conduct of all Soldiers within the command. Develops and executes NCO
Professional Development Programs within the command and advises/counsels Soldiers on
issues related to training, education, and professional development. Responsible for the unit’s
individual skills training program for all CMF’s
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Armor senior sergeants
must possess the following qualifications:
       (1) Physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
       (2) A physical profile of 222221.
       (3) Color discrimination of red/green.
       (4) Minimum score in aptitude area--N/A.
       (5) Qualifying scores.
             (a) A minimum score of 90 in aptitude area CO on Armed Services Vocational Aptitude
Battery (ASVAB) tests administered prior to 2 January 2002.
             (b) A minimum score of 87 in aptitude area CO on ASVAB tests administered on and
after 2 January 2002.
             (c) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power
Throw (PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
        (6) Per AR 600-8-19, promotion to MSG and SGM requires an interim secret eligibility or
higher.
    c. Reclassification.
         (1) Active Component. None authorized.
         (2) Reserve Component (RC). None authorized.
    d. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASIs associated
with all enlisted MOS)).
       (1) A8--Master Gunnery (M1/M1A1 Tank) (Rescind 202610).
       (2) J3--Bradley Master Gunner.
       (3) K8—Abrams Master Gunner (Effective 202610).
       (4) R7--Army Reconnaissance (Skill level 3 and above personnel only).
       (5) 5A--Joint Air Tactical Operations.
       (6) 5U--Tactical Air Operations.
       (7) C6—Cavalry Leader (Skill Level 5 only).
  e. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following tables:
       (1) Table 10-19Z-1. Physical requirements.
 (2) Table 10-19Z-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
(3) Table 10-19Z-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
